builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: NUMA-Torch: Compiler-Driven NUMA-Aware LLM Prefill on Multi-Socket CPUs
summary: The method replaces standard TorchInductor's NUMA-agnostic weight allocation and kernel scheduling with compiler-level NUMA-aware tensor parallelism that shards weights per socket and pins threads and allocations locally via CPU affinity. It requires a multi-socket CPU-only serving host, a modified TorchInductor toolchain, and weight sharding across sockets, adding compiler and deployment complexity. It can fail or be irrelevant on single-socket machines, on GPU-based serving where DRAM locality across sockets is not the bottleneck, and for operators lacking control over the compiler stack.
rationale: The reader's constrained setting centers on a single 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs, so a CPU multi-socket compiler optimization is not actionable now despite solid reported speedups.

claims.statement: The method replaces standard TorchInductor's NUMA-agnostic weight allocation and kernel scheduling with compiler-level NUMA-aware tensor parallelism that shards weights per socket and pins threads and allocations locally via CPU affinity. It requires a multi-socket CPU-only serving host, a modified TorchInductor toolchain, and weight sharding across sockets, adding compiler and deployment complexity. It can fail or be irrelevant on single-socket machines, on GPU-based serving where DRAM locality across sockets is not the bottleneck, and for operators lacking control over the compiler stack.
Prefill speedups of up to 2.63x on dual-socket Haswell, 1.87x on dual-socket Cascade Lake, and 2.27x on four-socket Haswell-EX versus standard TorchInductor.
